text:
Sahil: Heads-up — our hosted GPU usage signal spiked again this morning and the reserved commitment projection for Q4 looks like it will undershoot by ~18% if trends hold. Need quick triage and short-term smoothing ideas. :eyes:
Mia: Do we have region breakout? is this concentrated in APAC again?
Sahil: Primary pressure is us-west and eu-west. APAC is stable. See quick numbers below from the capacity alert.
capacity-bot: Daily summary: hosted qps +22% vs. last 7d; reserved utilization projection: 82% -> 67% by 11/01 if growth continues. Attached: /dashboards/hosted/reservations/2212347000
Jordan: Can you paste the simple calc? want to validate 18% figure.
Sahil: Simple calc: projected_token_hours = current_rate * 24 * 30; reserved_hours = committed_gpus * 24 * 30; gap_pct = (projected_token_hours - reserved_hours) / reserved_hours *100. Quick numbers: projected_token_hours=1.08e6, reserved_hours=9.1e5 -> gap ~18.7%
Aisha: Hmm. Two levers: short-term burst credits + temporary routing to lower-cost model variants for non-SLA traffic. Also can we throttle batch sizes for background embed jobs?
Mia: Agree on routing. We have a few noncritical routes with model=redwood-lite that can be downgraded for 12-48h. I'll list candidates.
Jordan: Billing side question: if we exceed committed reserved hours by ~20% for two weeks, what's the cost delta vs buying an extra reserved pool? (cc @finance)
Sahil: Rough: on-demand delta ~+45% per-token cost vs reserved; short extra reservation adds fixed monthly commit. For two weeks, on-demand with burst credits is cheaper. I'll run a quick cost calc.
Sahil: Quick shell calc I ran locally:
```
# rough numbers
reserved_monthly_cost=54000  # USD for committed pool
on_demand_hourly=12.5        # USD per GPU-hour
extra_needed_hours=1.7e5
extra_cost_on_demand = extra_needed_hours * on_demand_hourly
print(extra_cost_on_demand)  # ~= 2.1M (one-off hours) -> needs normalizing per token
```
Mia: That snippet is helpful but we should normalize per-token. Also note we get some credits for burst from our cloud vendor contract for Q4 (20k hours).
capacity-bot: Note: burst_credit_remaining=18300 hours in us-west, 7200 hours in eu-west.
Aisha: Next steps proposal: 1) Apply burst credits to us-west for next 72h. 2) Canary downgrade 3 noncritical routes to redwood-lite for background jobs. 3) Short-term reservation buy decision only if gap persists > 3 weeks.
Jordan: +1. Also add an ops play: auto-scale policy to cap hosted-slot requests for heavy embed jobs between 02:00-08:00 UTC for a week. That preserves peak SLOs while shaving bulk background cost.
Mia: I'll create the canary config PR for routing and add a label so we can revert quickly.
Sahil: I'll coordinate billing calc with finance and confirm burst credits allocation by EOD. If we still see >15% gap after 72h, we'll get procurement engaged for a temporary reserved add.
Aisha: Moving to action. Assigning owners: Mia (routing PR), Sahil (finance + procurement trigger), Jordan (auto-scale rule), I'll monitor dashboards and post updates. :thumbsup:
capacity-bot: Follow-ups scheduled: reservation-impact-check at 2212347600
